messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.01 MPa) water’s freezing (melting) point is only marginally below the standard 0 °C.  
Using the Clausius‑Clapeyron relation for the ice–water transition, the melting temperature at 10 kPa is roughly:

\[
T_{\text{freeze}} \;\approx\; 0.0^\circ\text{C} \;-\; 0.07^\circ\text{C}
\]

So the freezing point of water at 10 kPa is about **–0.07 °C** (essentially 0 °C for most practical purposes).
